title: Who the real worms are
source_text: Εἰ δὲ διὰ τὰ μὴ ἀρέσκοντα Κέλσῳ Χριστιανῶν καὶ Ἰουδαίων δόγματα. (ἃ) μηδὲ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐπίστασθαι φαίνεται. οὗτοι μὲν σκώληκες καὶ μύρμηκες οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ οὐ τοιοῦτοι. φέρε ἐξετάσωμεν καὶ τὰ αὐτόθεν πᾶσι προφαινόμενα δόγματα Χριστιανῶν καὶ Ἰουδαίων τοῖς τῶν λοιπῶν ἀνθρώπων, εἰ μὴ ἀναφανεῖται τοῖς ἅπαξ παραδεχομένοις εἶναί τινας ἀνθρώπους σκώληκας καὶ μύρμηκας ὅτι σκώληκες μὲν καὶ μύρμηκες καὶ βάτραχοι οἱ καταπεπτωκότες ἀπὸ τῆς περὶ θεοῦ ὑγιοῦς ὑπολήψεως φαντασίᾳ δ᾿ εὐσεβείας ἤτοι ἄλογα ζῷα ἢ ἀγάλματα σέβοντες ἢ καὶ τὰ δημιουργήματα, δέον ἐκ τοῦ κάλλους αὐτῶν θαυμάζειν τὸν πεποιηκότα κἀκεῖνον σέβειν, ἄνθρωποι δὲ καὶ εἴ τι ἀνθρώπων τιμιώτερον οἱ δυνηθέντες ἀναβῆναι ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ λόγῳ ἀπὸ λίθων καὶ ξύλων ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς νομιζομένης ὕλης εἶναι τιμιωτάτης ἀργύρου καὶ χρυσοῦ. ἀναβάντες δὲ καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐν κόσμῳ καλῶν ἐπὶ τὸν τὰ ὅλα ποιήσαντα καὶ ἐκείνῳ ἑαυτοὺς πιστεύσαντες καὶ ὡς μόνῳ διαρκεῖν δυναμένῳ ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ ὄντα καὶ ἐφορᾶν τοὺς πάντων λογισμοὺς καὶ ἀκούειν τῆς πάντων εὐχῆς τὰς εὐχὰς ἐκείνῳ ἀναπέμποντες καὶ ὡς ἐπὶ θεατοῦ αὐτοῦ τῶν γινομένων πάντα πράττοντες καὶ ὡς ἐπὶ ἀκροατοῦ τῶν λεγομένων φυλαττόμενοι λέγειν τὸ μὴ ἀρεσκόντως ἀπαγγελλόμενον τῷ θεῷ. εἰ μὴ ἄρα ἡ τηλικαύτη εὐσέβεια, οὔθ᾿ ὑπὸ πόνων οὔθ᾿ ὑπὸ κινδύνου θανάτου οὔθ᾿ ὑπὸ λογικῶν πιθανοτήτων νικωμένη. οὐδὲν βοηθεῖ τοῖς ἀνειληφόσιν αὐτὴν πρὸς τὸ μηκέτι αὐτοὺς παραβάλλεσθαι σκώληξιν, εἰ καὶ παρεβάλλοντο πρὸ τῆς τηλικαύτης εὐσεβείας· ἆρα δὲ οἱ νικῶντες τὴν δριμυτάτην πρὸς ἀφροδίσια ὄρεξιν, πολλῶν ποιήσασαν τοὺς θυμοὺς μαλθακοὺς καὶ κηρίνους, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο νικῶντες. ἐπείπερ ἐπείσθησαν μὴ ἄλλως οἰκειωθῆναι δύνασθαι τῷ θεῷ. ἐὰν μὴ καὶ διὰ σωφροσύνης ἀναβῶσι πρὸς αὐτὸν, σκωλήκων ἡμῖν δοκοῦσιν εἶναι ἀδελφοὶ καὶ μυρμήκων συγγενεῖς καὶ βατράχοις παραπλήσιοι; τί δὲ, τὸ λαμπρὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης. τηρούσης τὸ πρὸς τὸν πλησίον καὶ ὁμογενὲς κοινωνικὸν καὶ δίκαιον καὶ φιλάνθρωπον καὶ χρηστὸν, οὐδὲν ἀνύει πρὸς τὸ μὴ εἶναι νυκτερίδα τὸν τοιονδί; οἱ δὲ περὶ τὰς ἀκολασίας καλινδούμενοι, ὁποῖοί εἰσιν οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οἱ ταῖς χαμαιτύπαις ἀδιαφόρως προσιόντες διδάσκοντες δὲ καὶ μὴ πάντως παρὰ τὸ καθῆκον τοῦτο γίνεσθαι οὐκ εἰσὶν ἐν βορβόρῳ σκώληκες; καὶ μάλιστα συγκρινόμενοι τοῖς διδαχθεῖσι μὴ αἴρειν „τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ“ καὶ τὸ ὑπὸ τοῦ λόγου οἰκούμενον σῶμα καὶ ποιεῖν αὐτὰ „πόρνης μέλη,“ μαθοῦσι δὲ ἤδη καὶ (ὅτι) τὸ τοῦ λογικοῦ καὶ τῷ θεῷ τῶν ὅλων ἀνακείμενον „σῶμα“ „ναός ἐστι“ τοῦ προσκυνουμένου ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν θεοῦ, τοιοῦτον ἀπὸ τῆς καθαρᾶς περὶ τοῦ δημιουργοῦ ἐννοίας γινόμενον· οἳ καὶ φυλαττόμενοι διὰ τῆς παρανόμου συνουσίας φθείρειν „τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ“ ὡς εἰς θεὸν εὐσέβειαν ἀσκοῦσι τὴν σωφροσύνην.
pass_a_gloss: But if because of the doctrines (δόγμα) of Christians and Jews not pleasing (ἀρέσκω) to Celsus (which he appears not even at all [μηδὲ τὴν ἀρχήν] to understand, ἐπίσταμαι) these are worms (σκώληξ) and ants (μύρμηξ) but the rest not such, come (φέρε), let us examine (ἐξετάζω) also the doctrines of Christians and Jews evident straightaway (αὐτόθεν προφαίνομαι) to all, [compared] with those of the rest of men, whether it will not appear (ἀναφαίνομαι) to those who once (ἅπαξ) accept (παραδέχομαι) that some men are worms and ants, that worms and ants and frogs (βάτραχος) are those fallen (καταπίπτω) from the sound (ὑγιής) conception (ὑπόληψις) about God, and with an appearance (φαντασία) of piety (εὐσέβεια) revering (σέβω) either irrational animals (ἄλογα ζῷα) or statues (ἄγαλμα) or even the created works (δημιούργημα), when it is needful (δέον) from their beauty (κάλλος) to marvel at (θαυμάζω) the one who made [them] and revere him; but men, and whatever is more honourable (τιμιώτερος) than men, are those able to ascend (ἀναβαίνω), following the reason/word (ἀκολουθέω τῷ λόγῳ), from stones and woods and also from the matter (ὕλη) reckoned most honourable, silver and gold; and having ascended also from the beautiful things in the world (τὰ ἐν κόσμῳ καλά) to the one who made the whole (τὰ ὅλα), and having entrusted (πιστεύω) themselves to him, and as to the only one able to suffice (διαρκέω) for all beings and oversee (ἐφοράω) the reasonings (λογισμός) of all and hear the prayer of all, sending up (ἀναπέμπω) the prayers to him, and as before a spectator (θεατής) of what happens doing all things, and as before a hearer (ἀκροατής) of what is said guarding (φυλάσσομαι) against saying what is not pleasingly (ἀρεσκόντως) reported (ἀπαγγέλλω) to God. Unless indeed (εἰ μὴ ἄρα) such great (τηλικαύτη) piety, conquered (νικάω) neither by toils (πόνος) nor by danger of death nor by rational plausibilities (λογικαὶ πιθανότητες), helps (βοηθέω) nothing those who have taken it up (ἀναλαμβάνω) toward their being no longer compared (παραβάλλω) to worms, even if they were compared before such piety. And (ἆρα) do those who conquer the sharpest (δριμύτατος) appetite (ὄρεξις) for sexual pleasures (ἀφροδίσια), which has made the spirits (θυμός) of many soft (μαλθακός) and waxen (κήρινος), and conquering for this reason, since they were persuaded (πείθω) that they cannot otherwise be made own/akin (οἰκειόω) to God unless they ascend to him also through self-control (σωφροσύνη), seem to us to be brothers of worms and kin (συγγενής) of ants and like (παραπλήσιος) frogs? And what (τί δέ): the brightness (τὸ λαμπρόν) of justice/righteousness (δικαιοσύνη), keeping toward the neighbour (πλησίον) and kindred (ὁμογενής) the sociable (κοινωνικός) and just and humane (φιλάνθρωπος) and kind (χρηστός), achieves (ἀνύω) nothing toward such a one not being a bat (νυκτερίς)? But those rolling (καλινδέομαι) about licentiousnesses (ἀκολασία), such as are the many of men, and those approaching common prostitutes (χαμαιτύπη) indifferently (ἀδιαφόρως), and teaching also that this happens not at all (μὴ πάντως) contrary to what is fitting (τὸ καθῆκον), are they not worms in mire (βόρβορος)? And especially compared (συγκρίνω) with those taught not to take (αἴρω) ‘the members (μέλος) of Christ’ and the body inhabited (οἰκέω) by the Word (λόγος) and make them ‘members of a prostitute (πόρνη)’, and who have learned already also that the ‘body’ of the rational [being] (λογικός), dedicated (ἀνάκειμαι) to the God of the whole, ‘is a temple (ναός)’ of the God worshipped (προσκυνέω) by them, becoming such from the pure (καθαρός) notion (ἔννοια) about the Creator (δημιουργός); who also, guarding against corrupting/destroying (φθείρω) ‘the temple of God’ through unlawful intercourse, practise self-control as piety toward God.

pass_b_english: But if, because of the doctrines of Christians and Jews that displease Celsus (doctrines he seems not to understand at all), these people are worms and ants while the rest of mankind are not, come, let us examine the doctrines of Christians and Jews that are plain to everyone at first sight, and compare them with those of the rest of mankind. Let us see whether it will not become clear, to anyone who once grants that some human beings are worms and ants, who the worms and ants and frogs really are. They are those who have fallen away from a sound conception of God and, under a semblance of piety, worship irrational animals or images, or even the things that have been made (Romans 1:23, 25), when they ought to marvel at the Maker from the beauty of what he has made (Wisdom of Solomon 13:3–5) and to worship him. Human beings, on the other hand, and anything more honourable than human beings, are those who, following reason, have been able to rise above stones and wood, and even above silver and gold, the matter that is reckoned most precious. They have risen also from the beautiful things in the world to the one who made the universe and have entrusted themselves to him. They send up their prayers to him as the only one who is able to suffice for all that exists, to watch over the thoughts of all, and to hear the prayer of all. They do everything as in the sight of one who sees all that is done, and as before one who hears all that is said they take care to say nothing that, as it reaches God, would not please him.

Unless, of course, such great piety, which is overcome neither by sufferings nor by the danger of death nor by persuasive arguments, does nothing to keep those who have taken it up from being compared any longer to worms, even if they were so compared before they came to such piety! Take those who overcome the fiercest of appetites, the appetite for sexual pleasure, which has made the hearts of many soft as wax. They overcome it for this reason: they have been persuaded that they cannot otherwise be made God’s own unless they also rise to him through self-control. Do these seem to us to be brothers of worms, kin of ants, and like frogs? And what of the splendour of justice, which preserves fellowship, fairness, humanity and kindness toward one’s neighbour and fellow human being? Does it do nothing to keep such a person from being a bat?

But those who wallow in licentiousness, as most people do, and those who go to common prostitutes as a matter of indifference and even teach that this is not at all contrary to what is fitting, are they not worms in the mire? Above all when they are compared with those who have been taught not to take “the members of Christ” and the body in which the Word dwells and make them “members of a prostitute” (1 Corinthians 6:15)? These have learned already that the “body” of a rational being, dedicated to the God of the universe, “is a temple” of the God whom they worship (1 Corinthians 6:19), and that it becomes such through a pure conception of the Creator. Guarding against destroying “the temple of God” (1 Corinthians 3:17) through unlawful intercourse, they practise self-control as piety toward God.

choices.choice: Opening: removed added 'suppose Celsus holds'; kept the Greek 'if … come, let us examine' as one conditional sentence; 'displease Celsus' (Κέλσῳ as the one displeased)
φαντασίᾳ εὐσεβείας: 'under a show of piety' -> 'under a semblance of piety' (appearance, not necessarily hypocrisy)
Moved the Romans 1:23, 25 citation beside the worship of animals and created things, where the allusion lies
διαρκεῖν ἐπὶ πάντα: 'provide for' -> 'suffice for' all that exists
Justice clause: replaced stiff 'what is fellowly, just, humane and kind' with 'fellowship, fairness, humanity and kindness'; ὁμογενές -> 'fellow human being'
ἀδιαφόρως: 'without scruple' -> 'as a matter of indifference' (keeps the Stoic sense)
Restored καί between 'the members of Christ' and 'the body in which the Word dwells' (was turned into apposition); the question now ends with a question mark as in the Greek

Wisdom of Solomon 13:3–5 (knowing the Maker from the beauty of created things) and Romans 1:23, 25 (worshipping images of animals and the creature rather than the Creator) are allusions, not quotations; cited inline because the wording is close (κάλλος / τὸν πεποιηκότα; σέβοντες τὰ δημιουργήματα). 1 Corinthians 6:19 in Paul reads ‘a temple of the Holy Spirit within you’; Origen’s ‘temple of the God worshipped by them’ is his own adaptation, so only the quoted words σῶμα / ναός ἐστι are in quotation marks. ‘The body in which the Word dwells’ (τὸ ὑπὸ τοῦ λόγου οἰκούμενον σῶμα): λόγος capitalised as the indwelling Logos. ‘Following reason’ (ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ λόγῳ): λόγος here is reason, with Origen’s usual double sense of the divine Word. ‘μὴ πάντως παρὰ τὸ καθῆκον’: rendered ‘not at all contrary to what is fitting’; μὴ πάντως could also mean ‘not necessarily’; τὸ καθῆκον and ἀδιαφόρως are Stoic terms (duty; indifferent), probably aimed at Stoic teachers who allowed visits to prostitutes; not named, so no source is cited. ‘Soft as wax’ renders μαλθακοὺς καὶ κηρίνους; a proverbial phrase, source not certain, so uncited. Koetschau’s punctuation in the edition has a full stop after χρυσοῦ and after νικῶντες; Pass B follows the participial syntax across them. Bracketed (ἃ) in the first line is an editorial supplement and is followed.
